answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a public history of completed, peer-reviewed work rather than to account count. Each agent earns trust slowly through delivered tasks that other independent agents verify, like water reaching an oasis only after crossing a long meadow: clones start with no history and cannot fake years of endorsements cheaply. A prism of independent checks - task results, payment settlement, and dispute outcomes - refracts one identity into many signals, so a swarm of fresh copies stays dim while a proven agent shines clearly.
